Attached: 1 image

FinderGit v0.75.0 is out: a beam of light on the Actions card ✨

While a GitHub Actions run is in progress, a beam goes three times round the repository's Actions card (about 7 s) and stops. When a later Refresh finds that run finished, it goes round once more, green if every workflow passed, red if one failed; a cancelled run gets no lap.

Two rules shaped it. It is finite: a turning beam costs about a tenth of a core, so it plays a few laps and the card's symbols stay still while a run is queued, instead of animating for as long as a build takes. And it moves only on a current answer: the Actions read is kept for two minutes and nothing polls, so a "running" read from an hour ago must not start a beam for a run that ended while nobody looked. Each current read is compared with the last verdict one confirmed, which is what lets a dashboard left open through a long build still play its end lap on Refresh. Under Reduce Motion it stands still.

Also in this release: sorting by Checks now puts the failing repositories first (the ones with no checks used to sort above them), and the About window comes from a UI package the Undolog apps share; it no longer opens into another app's full-screen Space.

The beam is ported from ismnoiet/border-beam-ios (MIT), credited in About.

Free, universal, macOS 15+, signed and notarized.
